title: Antinuclear antibodies (ANA)
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It looks for antibodies that the immune system sometimes makes against your own cells.
why: For a possible autoimmune disease: joint pain, a rash, or a long-lasting fever with no clear cause.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in a few days, sometimes up to a week
tell_doctor: What medicines you take. Some of them affect the result
What symptoms you have and for how long
If anyone in your family has an autoimmune disease

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Best in the morning before eating, or a few hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: Past test results, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
The result is often given as a titer and a pattern. Your doctor will explain it
Results usually come in a few days. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Does a positive ANA mean I have a disease?
faq.a: No. A low titer can be found in healthy people. Your symptoms and other tests matter.

reminders.text: ANA test tomorrow. Best to come before eating. Water is fine.
